newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly up, heavy spreading late.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly up, heavy spreading late.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mostly higher with heavy bear spreading turning the nearby down and adding to gains in back months, traders said.

Scattered short covering had supported futures much of the day, but January fell late and March moved up to its day's high as a prominent local placed the bear spread, sources said. Traders had expected the spread to narrow further and at the close, it was $0.40 per thousand board feet apart.
Pressure in January again reflected the weak tone to cash lumber prices. Poor weather will limit construction and there is more than adequate lumber being offered, traders said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $398 per tbf, down $9 from both midweek and week-ago levels. Wholesale offerings had been running under the official quote and recent trade was quoted in the $375 to $390 area, cash sources said.

However, March was underpinned by expectations of increased demand from the housing sector in the spring and possible tighter supplies as the Canadian lumber quota ends its quota year. The quota year runs April 1 to the end of March the following year, they added.
Lumber closed off $0.20 per tbf to up $4.80 with only January off at $380.50 and March up most at $380.10 per tbf.
